title: 2024 Summer Olympics (part 1)
text: The 2024 Summer Olympics, officially the Games of the XXXIII Olympiad and branded as Paris 2024, were an international multi-sport event held in France from 26 July to 11 August 2024. Paris was the host city, with events also held in 16 additional cities across metropolitan France and one subsite in Tahiti, French Polynesia. Paris became the second city after London to host the Summer Olympics three times, having previously hosted in 1900 and 1924, exactly one hundred years earlier.

title: 2024 Summer Olympics (part 2)
text: The 2024 Games featured 329 events in 32 sports, including breaking (breakdancing), which made its Olympic debut as an optional sport. Around 10,500 athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees competed. The Games were the first to fully apply gender parity on the field of play, with an equal quota of male and female athletes. Surfing took place in Teahupo'o, Tahiti, nearly 16,000 kilometres from Paris, making it the most remote Olympic venue in history.

title: 2024 Summer Olympics opening ceremony
text: The opening ceremony of the 2024 Summer Olympics took place on 26 July 2024 along the Seine in Paris. It was the first Summer Olympics opening ceremony to be held outside a stadium: athletes were paraded by boat along a six-kilometre route through the centre of the city, passing landmarks such as Notre-Dame and the Louvre, and ending at the Trocadero facing the Eiffel Tower. Celine Dion closed the ceremony with a performance from the Eiffel Tower, her first public performance since announcing her illness.

title: 2024 Summer Olympics medal table
text: The United States topped the medal table of the 2024 Summer Olympics with 40 gold medals and 126 medals overall. China finished second, also with 40 golds but fewer total medals, marking the first time the top two nations tied on gold medals at a Summer Games. Japan finished third with 20 golds, followed by Australia with 18 and host nation France with 16 golds and 64 medals overall. A total of 92 National Olympic Committees won at least one medal.

title: Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics (part 1)
text: Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics was held over eleven days, comprising 48 events at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis and road events through the streets of Paris. For the first time the athletics programme achieved full gender parity in participation. The marathon course ran from the Hotel de Ville in Paris to Les Invalides, honouring the 1789 Women's March on Versailles, and a mass-participation marathon for amateurs was held on the same course.

title: Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics (part 2)
text: In the men's 100 metres final, Noah Lyles of the United States won gold in 9.784 seconds, beating Kishane Thompson of Jamaica by five thousandths of a second in one of the closest Olympic 100m finals ever. In the women's 100 metres, Julien Alfred won Saint Lucia's first ever Olympic medal, taking gold in 10.72 seconds ahead of American Sha'Carri Richardson. Lyles later took bronze in the 200 metres while competing with COVID-19, behind winner Letsile Tebogo of Botswana.

title: Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics (part 3)
text: Sweden's Armand Duplantis won the men's pole vault and broke his own world record with a clearance of 6.25 metres, one of the defining moments of the Games. Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone of the United States set a world record of 50.37 seconds in the women's 400 metres hurdles. In the men's 400 metres hurdles, Rai Benjamin finally won Olympic gold ahead of Karsten Warholm. Kenya's Faith Kipyegon became the first athlete to win three consecutive Olympic 1500 metres titles.

title: Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics (part 1)
text: Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics was held from 27 July to 4 August 2024 at the Paris La Defense Arena, a converted indoor stadium normally used for rugby and concerts, with marathon swimming events held in the Seine. The pool programme comprised 35 events, 17 each for men and women plus a mixed relay. The United States topped the swimming medal table with 8 gold medals, followed by Australia with 7.

title: Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics (part 2)
text: France's Leon Marchand was the standout swimmer of the Paris Games, winning four individual gold medals in the 200m butterfly, 200m breaststroke, and the 200m and 400m individual medley, setting Olympic records in all four. American Katie Ledecky won the 800m and 1500m freestyle, bringing her career total to nine Olympic gold medals, the most by any female swimmer. Pan Zhanle of China set a world record of 46.40 seconds in the men's 100m freestyle.

title: Gymnastics at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Gymnastics at the 2024 Summer Olympics was held at the Bercy Arena in Paris. Simone Biles of the United States returned from her withdrawal in Tokyo to win three gold medals, in the team event, the individual all-around, and the vault, plus a silver on floor exercise. Her teammate Suni Lee, the Tokyo all-around champion, took bronze in the all-around. Brazil's Rebeca Andrade won the floor exercise title ahead of Biles, becoming the most decorated Brazilian female Olympian.

title: Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: The basketball tournaments at the 2024 Summer Olympics were played in Lille and Paris. In the men's final, the United States beat host nation France 98-87 to win a fifth straight Olympic title, with Stephen Curry sealing the game with a series of late three-pointers. France's Victor Wembanyama starred for the hosts in his Olympic debut. The American women also beat France in their final, winning 67-66 for an eighth consecutive gold, the narrowest margin in a women's Olympic final.

title: Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: The tennis events of the 2024 Summer Olympics were played on the clay courts of Roland Garros in Paris. Novak Djokovic won the men's singles title, beating Carlos Alcaraz of Spain in straight sets in the final to complete a career Golden Slam at age 37, his first Olympic gold after three previous attempts. In the women's singles, Zheng Qinwen became the first Chinese player to win Olympic singles gold, defeating Donna Vekic of Croatia in the final.

title: Breaking at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Breaking made its Olympic debut at the 2024 Summer Olympics, held at the urban park at Place de la Concorde in Paris. Two events were contested, one for b-boys and one for b-girls, each featuring 16 athletes in one-on-one battles judged on technique, vocabulary, execution, musicality and originality. Ami Yuasa of Japan won the b-girls event and Phil Wizard of Canada won the b-boys event. Breaking is not on the programme for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

title: Surfing at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: The surfing competitions of the 2024 Summer Olympics were held at Teahupo'o on the island of Tahiti in French Polynesia, famous for its heavy barrelling wave. It was the most remote venue in Olympic history, located nearly 16,000 kilometres from the host city Paris. Kauli Vaast of France, who grew up surfing Teahupo'o, won the men's gold medal, and Caroline Marks of the United States won the women's event. A photograph of Brazilian surfer Gabriel Medina seemingly floating above the waves became one of the iconic images of the Games.

title: Judo at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Judo at the 2024 Summer Olympics was held at the Champ de Mars Arena in Paris, with 15 events contested. France's Teddy Riner won the men's heavyweight (+100 kg) category for a third individual Olympic title and then led the French mixed team to gold over Japan, cementing his status as one of the greatest judoka in history. Japan topped the judo medal table with three gold medals, while host France won two golds through Riner and the mixed team event.

title: Cycling at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Cycling at the 2024 Summer Olympics consisted of road, track, mountain bike and BMX events. Remco Evenepoel of Belgium achieved a historic double, winning both the men's individual time trial and the road race, the first rider to win both at a single Games. American Kristen Faulkner won a surprise gold in the women's road race. On the track at the Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines velodrome, the Netherlands' Harrie Lavreysen dominated the sprint events with three gold medals.

title: Fencing at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Fencing at the 2024 Summer Olympics took place in the Grand Palais in Paris, a Beaux-Arts exhibition hall built for the 1900 World's Fair, widely praised as one of the most spectacular venues of the Games. Twelve events were held, six for men and six for women. Hong Kong's Vivian Kong won the women's epee title, and Cheung Ka-long retained his men's foil title. France and Italy traditionally strong fencing nations both collected multiple medals in the historic setting.

title: 2024 Summer Olympics closing ceremony
text: The closing ceremony of the 2024 Summer Olympics took place on 11 August 2024 at the Stade de France, themed around a dystopian future in which the Olympic Games had disappeared. The Olympic flag was handed over to Los Angeles, host of the 2028 Games, in a segment featuring actor Tom Cruise abseiling into the stadium and carrying the flag, followed by performances by the Red Hot Chili Peppers, Billie Eilish and Snoop Dogg filmed in Los Angeles.

title: Olympic cauldron of the 2024 Summer Olympics
parent_title: Olympic cauldron of the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: The Olympic cauldron of the 2024 Summer Olympics took the form of a hot-air balloon that rose 60 metres above the Tuileries Garden in Paris every evening of the Games. For the first time in Olympic history the cauldron's flame was not a real fire: the ring of light used water mist and LED lighting to simulate flames, reflecting the Games' sustainability goals. The balloon paid homage to the first manned hydrogen balloon flight, made from the Tuileries in 1783. It proved so popular that it returns to the sky each summer.

title: Seine water quality at the 2024 Summer Olympics
parent_title: Seine water quality at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Water quality in the Seine was a persistent concern at the 2024 Summer Olympics, where the river hosted the triathlon swim legs and marathon swimming. France invested about 1.4 billion euros in cleaning the river, including a giant stormwater storage basin. Heavy rain during the opening days raised bacteria levels, forcing the postponement of triathlon training sessions and a one-day delay of the men's triathlon, though all swimming events in the river were ultimately completed.

title: Skateboarding at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Skateboarding at the 2024 Summer Olympics was held at the urban park at Place de la Concorde in Paris, with street and park events for men and women. Japan's Yuto Horigome defended his men's street title, and 14-year-old Coco Yoshizawa won the women's street event for Japan. Australia's Arisa Trew, also 14, won the women's park title, while Keegan Palmer of Australia retained the men's park crown. Skateboarding's young medallists were among the youngest competitors of the entire Games.

title: Sport climbing at the 2024 Summer Olympics
parent_title: Sport climbing at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: Sport climbing at the 2024 Summer Olympics was held at Le Bourget Climbing Venue near Paris. Unlike Tokyo's single combined event, Paris split the sport into two events per gender: a speed event and a boulder-and-lead combined event. Slovenia's Janja Garnbret defended her Olympic title in the women's boulder and lead, confirming her status as the greatest competition climber of her era. Britain's Toby Roberts won the men's combined event, and Sam Watson of the United States set a speed world record of 4.74 seconds en route to bronze.

title: France at the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: France competed at home at the 2024 Summer Olympics with 573 athletes, its largest delegation in a century. The host nation finished fifth in the medal table with 16 gold medals and 64 medals in total, its best performance at a Summer Games since 1900. Swimmer Leon Marchand became the face of the Games with four individual golds, judoka Teddy Riner won two more titles, and the men's rugby sevens team, led by Antoine Dupont, won France's first gold of the Games.

title: 2024 Summer Paralympics
text: The 2024 Summer Paralympics, the 17th Summer Paralympic Games, were held in Paris from 28 August to 8 September 2024. Around 4,400 athletes from 168 delegations competed in 549 medal events across 22 sports. It was the first time France hosted the Summer Paralympics. The opening ceremony was held outside a stadium at the Place de la Concorde and Champs-Elysees. China topped the medal table for the sixth consecutive Games, ahead of Great Britain and the United States.

title: Para athletics at the 2024 Summer Paralympics
parent_title: Para athletics at the 2024 Summer Paralympics
text: Para athletics at the 2024 Summer Paralympics was held at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, the same stadium used for Olympic athletics, with 164 medal events making it the largest sport on the Paralympic programme. Memorable performances included Switzerland's Catherine Debrunner winning five gold medals in wheelchair racing and setting multiple records, while host nation France celebrated sprint success in front of sell-out crowds that gave the Paralympics record attendance figures.

title: Para swimming at the 2024 Summer Paralympics
parent_title: Para swimming at the 2024 Summer Paralympics
text: Para swimming at the 2024 Summer Paralympics took place at the Paris La Defense Arena from 29 August to 7 September 2024, with 141 medal events. Italy's Simone Barlaam and the Netherlands' teenage swimmer Rogier Dorsman were among the multiple gold medallists, while Britain's Maisie Summers-Newton defended her breaststroke and medley titles. The venue, shared with Olympic swimming, drew large crowds throughout and several world records fell during the nine days of competition.

title: Wheelchair tennis at the 2024 Summer Paralympics
parent_title: Wheelchair tennis at the 2024 Summer Paralympics
text: Wheelchair tennis at the 2024 Summer Paralympics was played on the clay courts of Roland Garros in Paris, the venue of the Olympic tennis tournament and the French Open. Japan's Tokito Oda, aged 18, won the men's singles title, beating Britain's Alfie Hewett in the final. The Netherlands' Diede de Groot continued her domination of the women's game by winning singles gold. Niels Vink of the Netherlands won the quad singles title to complete a strong Dutch showing.

title: Olympic Village of the 2024 Summer Olympics
parent_title: Olympic Village of the 2024 Summer Olympics
text: The Olympic and Paralympic Village of the 2024 Games was built across the Seine-Saint-Denis communes of Saint-Denis, Saint-Ouen-sur-Seine and L'Ile-Saint-Denis, north of Paris. Designed as a low-carbon district, it housed around 14,500 residents during the Olympics and relied on geothermal and water-based cooling instead of conventional air conditioning, a choice that drew complaints during hot spells and led some delegations to bring portable units. After the Games the village is being converted into housing and offices for about 6,000 residents.
